steps.label: What B-cells are
steps.why: B cells are the only cells that make antibodies, so the whole of humoral immunity runs through them.
common_mistakes: Calling B cells phagocytes. They make antibodies; they do not engulf.
Confusing B cells with T cells.
steps.memory_tip: B for bone marrow and for antiBody.

steps.label: Immunocompetent B-cells
steps.why: A mature B cell carries its antibody on the outside like a hook, so it can catch the one antigen it was made for.
common_mistakes: Writing that mature B cells release antibodies. They carry them on the surface.
steps.memory_tip: Antibodies on the surface make the cell immunocompetent.
steps.margin_note: Say where the antibodies sit at this stage.

steps.label: Memory and plasma cells
steps.why: One kind fights the infection now and the other remembers it, which is why the second attack by the same germ is dealt with faster.
common_mistakes: Giving memory cells the antibody-making job. Plasma cells do that.
Leaving out the quicker second response.
steps.memory_tip: Plasma cells fight today, memory cells remember for next time.
steps.margin_note: End with the quick second response. That is the point.
